attractions.name: Donsol Whale Shark (Butanding) Interaction
attractions.summary: Donsol is world-renowned for ethical whale shark (butanding) snorkeling interactions in Donsol Bay, conducted under WWF-developed guidelines. Snorkeling only is allowed (no scuba, no touching or feeding), with a trained Butanding Interaction Officer (BIO) and up to six swimmers per boat. Sightings are of wild animals and are not guaranteed.
attractions.how_to_get_there: Fly to Legazpi (Bicol/LGP), then take a van or bus to Donsol (about 1.5 to 2 hours); or travel from Sorsogon City by public transport. Register in person at the Donsol Butanding Interaction Center in Brgy. Dancalan.
attractions.best_time: Season runs roughly November to May or June, with the highest sighting rates typically February to April; early-morning trips are recommended.
attractions.fees: Interaction/registration fee about PHP 300 for foreigners and PHP 100 for Filipinos; boat rental about PHP 3,500 (maximum 6 swimmers, includes a Butanding Interaction Officer). Cash only.
attractions.notes: Rates per tour-operator and travel-guide sources (2024-2025); confirm current rates and season status with the Donsol Municipal Tourism Office before travel. Booking/registration is done in person at the Butanding Interaction Center (Brgy. Dancalan). Donsol also offers scuba diving and, in season, manta ray sightings.

attractions.name: Bulusan Volcano Natural Park & Bulusan Lake
attractions.summary: A DENR-protected eco-park on the slopes of active Mt. Bulusan, centered on Bulusan Lake, a spring-fed crater-side lake ringed by rainforest. Popular activities include kayaking on the lake, a shaded lakeside nature/forest trail, and birdwatching. Visitors register and pay fees at the park's Ecotourism Center.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City, ride a jeep or van bound for Bulusan (about 1 hour), then charter a tricycle to Bulusan Lake (about 15 to 20 minutes). Register at the Ecotourism Center; a shuttle or a 20 to 30 minute walk reaches the lake and park entrance.
attractions.best_time: Open daily about 7:30 AM to 5:00 PM; the dry months (roughly December to May) are best for clear trails and kayaking.
attractions.fees: Entrance about PHP 50 (about PHP 25 for students, PWDs, seniors, Bulusan residents, and young children) plus a PHP 10 environmental fee; parking from about PHP 20 (motorcycle) up to PHP 150 (bus). Kayak rental extra.
attractions.notes: Fees per travel-guide sources (2023-2024); confirm at the Ecotourism Center. Mt. Bulusan is an active volcano; check the PHIVOLCS alert level and LGU/DENR advisories, as the park or lake may close during volcanic unrest.

attractions.name: Mount Bulusan Summit Trek
attractions.summary: Mt. Bulusan (about 1,565 masl) is an active stratovolcano and the centerpiece of Bulusan Volcano Natural Park, its slopes shared among Bulusan, Irosin, Juban, and Casiguran. The challenging summit hike climbs through mossy forest and is protected under DENR as a national park; a local guide is mandatory and some itineraries begin with a kayak crossing of Bulusan Lake.
attractions.how_to_get_there: Access via Bulusan or Irosin; coordinate registration and a mandatory guide through the Bulusan Volcano Natural Park Ecotourism Center or LGU tourism office.
attractions.best_time: Dry season (roughly March to May), and only when the PHIVOLCS alert is Level 0 and trails are officially open.
attractions.fees: Registration about PHP 350 per person and a guide fee about PHP 1,000 per day (roughly 5:1 hiker-to-guide ratio) per hiking-community sources; confirm with the LGU.
attractions.notes: Active volcano: climbs are frequently suspended and a 4-km Permanent Danger Zone applies during unrest. Always verify the current PHIVOLCS alert level and secure permits and a guide through Bulusan or Irosin LGU tourism before planning. Figures from hiking-community sources; dates vary.

attractions.name: Subic Beach (Matnog)
attractions.summary: Subic Beach on Calintaan Island off Matnog is famous for its pinkish sand, created by crushed red organ-pipe coral mixing with white sand, and clear turquoise water. It is the highlight of the Matnog island-hopping circuit, which also takes in Tikling Island, the Juag Lagoon fish sanctuary, and a sea cave.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City's SITEX terminal, take a minibus or van to Matnog (about PHP 130). Go to the Matnog Tourism Office near the port to arrange a boat; Subic Beach is a short banca ride away.
attractions.best_time: Dry season (roughly March to May); the Matnog Tourism Office is open daily about 6:30 AM to 4:30 PM.
attractions.fees: Island-hopping boat about PHP 1,600 for a day trip (up to 10 passengers) or about PHP 2,000 overnight; registration about PHP 50 (local), PHP 40 (senior), PHP 300 (foreigner). Cottage or tent rental extra.
attractions.notes: Fees per travel-guide sources (2024); confirm at the Matnog Tourism Office. Matnog is also the ferry port to Samar and the Visayas.

attractions.name: Juag Lagoon Marine Sanctuary (Matnog)
attractions.summary: Juag Lagoon is a community fish sanctuary near Subic Beach in Matnog where visitors feed and snorkel among large reef fish and other marine life such as groupers, snappers, Napoleon wrasse, and giant clams kept in netted enclosures. It is a standard stop on the Matnog island-hopping tour.
attractions.how_to_get_there: Included in the Matnog island-hopping circuit; arrange the boat at the Matnog Tourism Office near the port, reached by minibus or van from Sorsogon City's SITEX terminal (about PHP 130).
attractions.best_time: Dry season (roughly March to May) for calmer seas.
attractions.fees: About PHP 200 per boat entrance plus fish food; optional snorkeling with gear about PHP 200 per person (per travel-guide sources). Separate from the island-hopping boat fee.
attractions.notes: Fees per travel-guide sources; confirm on site. Handle marine life responsibly and follow sanctuary rules.

attractions.name: Rizal Beach (Gubat)
attractions.summary: Rizal Beach is a long, wide stretch of fine light-beige to white sand facing the Pacific in Gubat, one of Sorsogon's most accessible beaches. Its gently sloping shore suits families and wading, while its rideable waves have helped make Gubat a growing surf destination. Rizal Beach Resort and other lodgings line the shore.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Manila, take a Gubat-bound bus (for example Penafrancia) and alight at Gubat town proper, then a tricycle to Rizal Beach; or from Sorsogon City's SITEX terminal take a van to Gubat (about PHP 56) then a tricycle.
attractions.best_time: Year-round for swimming; surf is generally best in the northeast-monsoon months (roughly October to March).
attractions.fees: No fee for the public beach; Rizal Beach Resort charges an entrance fee (reported around PHP 40 per person) with table and cottage rentals extra, per travel sources.
attractions.notes: Resort entrance fee cited from a 2020 community post; confirm current rates. Rizal Beach (Brgy. Rizal) is a separate area from the Buenavista surf camps.

attractions.name: Lola Sayong Eco-Surf Camp & Gubat Surfing
attractions.summary: Lola Sayong Eco-Surf Camp in Brgy. Buenavista, Gubat, is Sorsogon's best-known surf spot, offering beginner-to-intermediate reef breaks, board rental, and lessons in a low-key eco-farm setting with nipa-hut lodging. Gubat's consistent left and right reef breaks have made it a rising Bicol surf destination.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City's SITEX terminal, take a van to Gubat (about PHP 56), then a tricycle (about PHP 60) to Brgy. Buenavista. The nearest airport is Legazpi (LGP).
attractions.best_time: Surf season is typically the northeast (amihan) monsoon, roughly September or October to March.
attractions.notes: Board rental and lesson rates vary and were not confirmed by a fetched source; arrange directly with the camp (website lolasayong.org). Rizal Beach (Brgy. Rizal) and the Buenavista surf camps are in different barangays.

attractions.name: San Benon / Mateo Hot and Cold Springs (Irosin)
attractions.summary: A geothermal spring resort at the foot of Mt. Bulusan in Irosin (Brgy. Monbon), long known locally as San Benon and now operating as Mateo Hot and Cold Springs Resort. It features man-made pools mixing naturally hot sulfuric, lukewarm, and cool spring water, plus a restaurant and cottages.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City, take a van or bus to Irosin, then a tricycle to Brgy. Monbon (San Benon / Mateo Springs).
attractions.best_time: Open daily for day and evening swims; hours vary by source, so confirm locally.
attractions.fees: Entrance reported around PHP 65 (day) and PHP 75 (night) in older sources, with more recent reports of about PHP 100 to 130 per person plus a minimum cottage rental (around PHP 500).
attractions.notes: Fees are from travel blogs (2022-2024) and may be outdated; confirm before visiting. Informal contact numbers and an email that circulate on travel blogs were dropped as unverifiable, and the resort's former website (sanbenonresort.com) is no longer active. Confirm details in person or via the Irosin LGU tourism office.

attractions.name: Barcelona Church & Ruins (St. Joseph Parish)
attractions.summary: The St. Joseph Parish Church in Barcelona, commonly called Barcelona Church, is a fortress-like coral-stone church completed by Franciscan missionaries in 1874 and considered among the oldest in the Bicol Region. Across from it, facing Gubat Bay, stand the stone ruins of the old Presidencia building and a Spanish-era fort and lighthouse.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Gubat, take a jeepney or tricycle to Barcelona town proper; the church sits near the shoreline. Barcelona is south of Gubat along the coastal road.
attractions.best_time: Daytime; the seaside ruins are especially pleasant in the late afternoon.
attractions.notes: Construction date (1874) and the coral-stone building method bound with lime, egg white, and tuba are per travel and heritage sources. An active parish; be respectful during Mass.

attractions.name: Paguriran Island & Lagoon (Bacon, Sorsogon City)
attractions.summary: Paguriran Island is a rocky islet off Brgy. Sawanga in the Bacon district of Sorsogon City, enclosing a natural saltwater lagoon that fills at high tide and can be walked or waded at low tide. The mainland shore has sand, cottages, and cliff views and is popular for day trips.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City, drive via the Diversion Road toward Bacon and Brgy. Sawanga (a bit over an hour), or take a jeepney to Bacon town proper then onward to Sawanga.
attractions.best_time: Dry season (roughly March to May); the lagoon is best at higher tide, so check tide timing.
attractions.fees: Reported entrance about PHP 50, parking about PHP 40, and cottage rental from about PHP 200 (per travel sources).
attractions.notes: Fees per travel blogs; confirm on site. Reaching the island itself may require a short boat ride or a low-tide crossing.

attractions.name: Kasanggayahan Festival
attractions.summary: Kasanggayahan is Sorsogon's province-wide cultural, historical, and religious festival held throughout October, commemorating the creation of Sorsogon as a province separate from Albay in 1894. The name comes from an old Bikol word for prosperity and abundance; events include street dancing, agro-trade fairs, pageants, and historical rites. It was first celebrated in 1974.
attractions.how_to_get_there: Main events center on Sorsogon City (Capitol grounds and city plaza); reach the city via Legazpi airport then van or bus.
attractions.best_time: Every October; October 17 is observed as the province's founding-anniversary holiday.
attractions.notes: Sources differ on the exact 1894 date: the provincial government (sorsogon.gov.ph) cites October 29, 1894 as the separation from Albay while observing October 17 as the founding-anniversary holiday, whereas Wikipedia and news sources cite October 17, 1894. First celebrated in 1974 (the province's 80th foundation anniversary) per the provincial government. The exact yearly program is set by the Provincial Tourism, Culture and Arts Office (PTCAO).

attractions.name: Pili Festival (Sorsogon City)
attractions.summary: The Pili Festival is Sorsogon City's annual celebration of the pili nut, a tree indigenous to Bicol, held around June 28 to 29 together with the city fiesta honoring patrons Saints Peter and Paul. It features street dancing, floats, and showcases of pili-based products and delicacies. It was first staged in 2000.
attractions.how_to_get_there: Centered in Sorsogon City; reach the city via Legazpi airport then van or bus.
attractions.best_time: Around June 28 to 29 each year (the city fiesta of Sts. Peter and Paul).
attractions.notes: Date and 2000 founding per city tourism and festival sources; confirm the current-year program with the city or provincial tourism office.

attractions.name: Pili Nuts & Pasalubong (Where to Buy)
attractions.summary: Pili is Sorsogon's signature product: the buttery nut is sold roasted, glazed or caramelized (mazapan), and in tarts and other sweets, while the pulp yields cooking oil and the tree also supports soaps and other goods. Pasalubong (souvenir food) shops cluster in Sorsogon City and along the Maharlika/AH26 Bicol South Road, plus public markets, terminals, and malls.
attractions.how_to_get_there: Widely available in Sorsogon City; shops line the national highway (AH26) and the public market.
attractions.notes: Named outlets include Edgeline's Pili Products & Pasalubong Shop and Leslie's Pili Farm (Brgy. Bibincahan, Sorsogon City) per news and travel sources; many market and highway vendors also sell pili. Verify shop hours and locations before visiting.

attractions.name: Donsol Firefly River Cruise
attractions.summary: An evening boat cruise on the Ogod (Donsol) River to watch thousands of fireflies light up the riverside mangroves and trees. Small wooden boats (about six passengers) with a boatman and guide depart after dark; it is a popular complement to daytime whale shark trips.
attractions.how_to_get_there: The firefly boat terminal is about 3 km east of Donsol town, where the Ogod River meets Dawitan Road; arrange through the Donsol Municipal Tourism Office.
attractions.best_time: After dark, roughly 7 to 9 PM; best on clear, moonless nights.
attractions.fees: About PHP 1,250 per boat (up to about six passengers); some operators price around PHP 600 per person (per travel-guide sources).
attractions.notes: Rates per travel-guide sources; confirm with the Donsol Municipal Tourism Office. Firefly numbers vary with weather and season.

attractions.name: Palogtoc Falls
attractions.summary: Palogtoc (Palogtok) Falls is a waterfall fed by Mt. Bulusan's waters, located in Brgy. San Roque, Bulusan at the foot of the volcano. It is reached by a short walk through coconut plantations from the Mt. Bulusan trailhead and offers a natural pool for a cool dip.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City's SITEX terminal, take a minibus or van to Bulusan, then a tricycle toward Brgy. San Roque; from where the road ends it is a short walk (about 500 m, roughly 15 to 20 minutes) through coconut groves to the falls.
attractions.best_time: Dry season (roughly March to May) for safer trails and clearer water.
attractions.notes: Located in Brgy. San Roque, Bulusan at the foot of Mt. Bulusan per travel-guide sources including a 2025 guide; some older sources loosely describe it as being between Irosin and Bulusan. Trails can be muddy and slippery after rain, and a local guide is helpful. A small on-site entrance fee applies but is not listed here; confirm on site.

attractions.name: Prieto Diaz Mangrove Ecopark
attractions.summary: An award-winning community mangrove ecopark in Prieto Diaz protecting roughly 300 hectares of restored mangrove forest with about 19 mangrove species, along with corals and birdlife. Visitors can take guided eco-tours, paddle or kayak through channels, and birdwatch; the town is regarded as a Bicol eco-tourism model.
attractions.how_to_get_there: From Sorsogon City, travel to Prieto Diaz (northeast of the city) by jeepney or van, then continue to the mangrove ecopark; arrange guides through the LGU.
attractions.best_time: Dry season (roughly December to May); early morning is best for birdwatching.
attractions.notes: Entrance and guide fees were not confirmed by a fetched source; confirm with the Prieto Diaz LGU or tourism office. Protected-area size and species counts per travel and news sources.

attractions.name: Balay Buhay sa Uma Bee Farm
attractions.summary: Balay Buhay sa Uma is an agri-tourism bee farm, restaurant, and resort in Brgy. San Roque, Bulusan, set among honeybee hives and gardens with a natural cold spring pool. Visitors can tour the apiary, learn about beekeeping, sample honey products, dine, and swim.
attractions.how_to_get_there: In Brgy. San Roque, Bulusan, near the route toward Bulusan Volcano Natural Park; reach Bulusan by van or bus from Sorsogon City, then a tricycle.
attractions.best_time: Open daily about 8 AM to 5 PM.
attractions.fees: Entrance about PHP 50 (with a food purchase) or about PHP 100 (farm tour), per travel sources.
attractions.notes: Fees and contact per travel blogs and the farm's own listings (2021-2023); confirm current details before visiting.
